display.title: Episode 538: The Rambam's Grave (The Three Weeks)
display.summary_short: A Three Weeks show without music: why we ask 'Ad masai?', and the life of the Rambam, ending with the miracle of the camel that led his funeral caravan to Teveria.
display.summary_long: Broadcast in the first week of the Three Weeks, 5752, and opened without music. Uncle Yossi explains Asarah B'Teves, Shiva Asar B'Tammuz and Tisha B'Av, and says that while we ask Hashem 'Ad masai, how much longer?', Hashem asks us the same: let us be ready for Moshiach by learning more Torah and doing more mitzvos. He also passes on the Rebbe's call for everyone to learn Rambam daily. The story tells the life of the Rambam: born in Cordova, forced to flee at 14, wandering to Morocco, surviving a storm at sea, visiting Yerushalayim and Chevron, and finally settling in Egypt, where he wrote the Mishneh Torah and the Thirteen Principles of Faith. When he passed away, cities competed for the honor of his burial. On the way through the desert, robbers attacked the funeral caravan, but those who tried to touch the coffin fell lifeless, and the rest fled. Then the camel walked on by itself, as if led by an unseen hand, until it knelt in a field in Teveria. Two brothers lead the Shema in between. The show ends with a prayer for the Rebbe's recovery.
display.lesson: Hashem never sleeps and always guards Klal Yisrael; during the Three Weeks we prepare for Moshiach by learning more Torah, including the Rambam.
